title: Tenant Protection Act annual rent cap (Civ. Code § 1947.12)

title: Massachusetts notice to terminate tenancy at will
requirement: Either party may end a tenancy at will with three months' written notice; if rent is payable at intervals shorter than three months, notice equal to the payment interval or 30 days, whichever is longer, suffices. Nonpayment allows 14 days' notice to quit, with a 10-day right to cure.

coverage_conditions: Tenancies at will in Massachusetts; the section states no building, unit or owner limits.
exemptions: A tenant who received a similar notice to quit within the preceding 12 months has no right to prevent termination by paying the rent due.
quoted_span: Estates at will may be determined by either party by three months' notice in writing for that purpose given to the other party; and, if the rent reserved is payable at periods of less than three months, the time of such notice shall be sufficient if it is equal to the interval between the days of payment or thirty days, whichever is longer.
penalty: If a nonpayment notice omits the required notification, the tenant's cure period is extended to the day the answer is due in an eviction action.
